term: Serving Frameworks (vLLM, SGLang, TensorRT-LLM, TGI, llama.cpp
definition: The inference engines implementing the techniques above: vLLM and SGLang as high-throughput open standards, TensorRT-LLM for maximum NVIDIA performance, llama.cpp/Ollama for local and edge deployment.
details: The inference engines implementing the techniques above: vLLM and SGLang as high-throughput open standards, TensorRT-LLM for maximum NVIDIA performance, llama.cpp/Ollama for local and edge deployment. Framework choice sets your ceiling on throughput per GPU.

explainer.lead: These are the inference engines that implement modern serving techniques for LLMs. The framework choice sets your ceiling on throughput per GPU.

tiers.eli5: Like choosing the delivery van for a shop: some haul more per trip, some are better for small local runs.
tiers.practitioner: vLLM and SGLang serve as high-throughput open standards, TensorRT-LLM targets maximum NVIDIA performance, and llama.cpp/Ollama suit local and edge deployment. Pitfall: the wrong framework caps throughput per GPU.
tiers.paperLevel: Classification of inference engines by role: high-throughput open standards (vLLM, SGLang), maximum NVIDIA performance (TensorRT-LLM), local and edge deployment (llama.cpp/Ollama).

explainer.example: Picking TensorRT-LLM for maximum NVIDIA GPU throughput versus llama.cpp for edge hardware.
